key_insight: DashAttention replaces fixed top-k selection with a differentiable, per-query adaptive sparse routing mechanism so the model learns how many and which key–value tokens to attend to, preserving gradient flow across sparse and dense stages.
problem_solved: Fixed top-k hierarchical attention assumes a constant number of relevant tokens and blocks gradient flow between coarse (block) selection and fine-grained attention, limiting accuracy and end-to-end optimization for long-context transformers.
method: Differentiable hierarchical routing: use a continuous relaxation (learned gating/soft allocation) to score and select KV blocks and tokens so selection is end-to-end differentiable.
Adaptive per-query sparsity: dynamically allocate attention budget per query rather than a fixed k, allowing the model to attend to variable numbers of relevant tokens depending on context.

Two-stage fine-grained attention with gradient flow: coarse block selection followed by dense attention on selected tokens while allowing gradients to flow back into the coarse selector for joint optimization and efficiency.
impact: Enables more accurate, efficient long-context attention by learning when and how much to sparsify; practical for scaling transformers with better compute-accuracy trade-offs and simpler end-to-end training.
